newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian debt issues rise in September - PRIME.
newsitem.headline: Indian debt issues rise in September - PRIME.

text.p: Indian debt issues continued in September its recent dominance of the equities market, PRIME, which monitors the country's primary markets, said on Tuesday.
It said that however, unlike earlier when financial institutions were major players, debt issues this time were from the private sector: TISCO, L&T and Arvind Mills.

"Interestingly, all these three issues went for bookbuilding, offering an aggregate amount of 7,600 million rupees through this route and keeping an amount of 3,400 million rupees through public issues," the data firm said in its monthly review of the market.
Regrettably, it said, these three issues were unable to garner sufficient interest either at the institutional or at the retail level.

PRIME said the response to the other issues of the month too were poor. "Of the issues which opened in first half September, several have had to take their issues till the last closing dates," it said.

Given the market scenario, PRIME said it was of the view that only the public sector is expected to dominate the immediate future with IDBI (10,000 million rupees), ICICI (10,000 million rupees) and Konkan railway (1,500 million rupees) planning to soon hit the market with debt issues.

Amongst mega premia equity issues, BPCL has already decided to pull out its forthcoming 4,500 million rupees issue and only Dena Bank's 1,800 million rupees issue is likely in the near-term. Planned are issues of Canara Bank (10,000 million rupees) and Bank of Baroda (10,000 million rupees).
The only planned private sector mega public issues are expected from Amitabh Bacchhan Corp (2,250 million rupees), DLF Power (1,950 million rupees) and Amer Ship Management (1,070 million rupees).

Total mobilisation, from public debt issues in September aggregated 6,390 million rupees, much higher than 3,480 million rupees in August though lower than 16,740 million rupees in July, 6,840 million rupees in June and 6,750 million rupees in May. It was higher than 3,830 million rupees in April.

The number of issues continued at a higher level with as many as 87 companies tapping the market in September. This was almost similar to 86 issues in August though lower than 99 issues in July and 127 issues during June. In the earlier months, there were 73 issues in May and 105 in April, PRIME said.

The September month -- against three in May, 10 in June and five each in July and August -- had four issues of 100 million rupees plus, these being from TISCO (1,500 million rupees), L&T (1,500 million rupees), Arvind Mills (400 million rupees) and Suryalakshmi Cotton Mills (147.80 million rupees).
PRIME said September witnessed a flurry of small issues; 42 of the 87 issues (48 percent) were below 30 million rupees, of which four were even less than 10 million rupees.

Worse, the dominance of issues from finance companies continued with as many as 32 of the 87 issues (37 percent) being from this sector, quite like 40 percent in August though unlike 26 to 29 percent in April - July period, it said.
During the month, GTC Global and Zytel Investments' issues were withdrawn on the eve of its opening, bringing the total since April to 21 cancelled or withdran issues.
Premium issues continued to few. Only nine of the 87 issues in September (11 out of 86 in August, eight out of 99 in July) were offered at a premium.
